note: The fuzzer-provided bytes are parsed into a module whose only function has a non-void result type and an unreachable body.
The input-controlled code segment containing the unreachable instruction is selected for AOT compilation.
The selected code segment and its function type are queued for FunctionCompiler.
Compilation of the input instruction sequence marks the current function body unreachable and leaves no concrete return value on Stack.
After compiling an unreachable non-void body, the compiler still unconditionally emits a normal return instead of preserving unreachable state or synthesizing an undef return value.
The non-void return path requires one LLVM value and invokes stackPop even though Stack is empty for this candidate.
stackPop reads the back element of an empty Stack vector, triggering the sanitizer-detected segmentation fault.
